summary: _(c) Hold and declare that the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs. 175.77 Crore/upwards on total cost of project along with carrying cost applicable from the date the aforesaid amount becomes payable till the actual date of payment, towards compensation for such Change in Law events to the Petitioner._ 6. The instant petition was filed on 21.07.2023. During the hearing held on 22.09.2023, after considering NGEL’s submissions, the Commission admitted the petition and directed the parties to file their replies and rejoinders. During the hearing held on 03.01.2024, the Commission again permitted the Respondents, Telangana Discoms, to file their reply, and NGEL was thereafter permitted to file its rejoinder. On 02.07.2025, on the request of the Respondents, the Commission adjourned the matter to the next date. During the hearing on 10.09.2025, NGEL submitted that the pleadings were complete and that the issues involved were squarely covered by the previous orders of the Commission. The matter may be reserved for order with both sides permitted to file their written submissions, if any. Whereas, the Respondents, Telangana Discoms, prayed for another opportunity of an oral hearing. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission adjourned the matter with a direction to both sides to file their written submissions/ notes of arguments. During the hearing held on 10.11.2025, the contracting parties made detailed submissions and concluded their respective arguments. The matter was reserved for order with the direction to both sides to file the written submissions, if any. - a) At the outset is submitted that the present petition is misconceived, not maintainable in law and liable to be dismissed _in limine_ . - d) The notices dated 19.07.2022, 04.11.2022 & 16.11.2022 issued by NGEL informing about the Change in Law events indicated that the said impact, which shall be passthrough in Usage Charges, would be informed separately in due course along with details of expenditure towards BCD and GST and necessary documents. However, to date, no such information has been shared with the Respondents, and in fact, vide the letter dated 16.11.2022, NGEL intimated the Respondents that it was approaching the Commission by filing a petition seeking compensation. In light of the above, the contention of NGEL that Respondents did not respond to any of the notices is vehemently opposed, since NGEL failed to furnish complete details along with supporting documents for verification by the DISCOMs, and also the corresponding change/ revision in usage charges in view of this Change in Law impact was also not communicated by NTPC/NGEL. - c) The Respondents lodged no contemporaneous objection with MNRE or SECI at the time when the extensions were granted. The O.M.s of 13.08.2020, 29.06.2021, and 02.06.2021, and the SCoD extensions that followed, remained unchallenged by the Respondents for years and drew power from all these projects. Their present plea that they “ought to have been consulted” is therefore an afterthought, unsupported by any record of protest during the critical period. The Respondents’ belated letter relied upon in their reply cannot override or dilute binding ministerial and nodal-agency decisions taken much earlier. 12. We have heard the learned counsels for NGEL (the Petitioner) and Respondents and have carefully perused the records and considered the submissions of the parties. 18. From the above, we observe that NGEL has already informed the Respondents about the extension of time in SCoD under different circumstances. We observe that the present petition is limited to seeking a declaration of change in law and consequential reliefs. In view of the above, we are of the view that the objections raised by the Respondents are beyond the scope of the instant petition. _84. It is in the above context that we accept that the regulatory powers of the Central Commission ought to have been properly exercised to do complete justice to the claims for compensation it having been denied by depriving the SPPDs of their legitimate expectation of relief vis-à-vis the burden of carrying cost as well, rendering the dispensation partially unfair._ _project. The Commission has articulated its views on the subject as under (quoted from Order dated 27.03.2020 which is subject matter of appeal no. 131 of 2022):_ 39. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, in its Order dated 12.12.2022, in Civil Appeal no. 8880/2022 in the case of _“Telangana Northern Power Distribution Co. Limited & Anr. Vs. Parampujya Solar Energy Pvt. Limited & Ors.”_ (and in similar Orders dated 03.01.2023 and 23.01.2023) has held as under: - _“Pending further orders, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) shall comply with the directions issued in paragraph 109 of the impugned order dated 15 September 2022 of the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity. However, the final order of the CERC shall not be enforced pending further orders.”_ - e) The directions issued in this Order so far as they relate to compensation for the period post Commercial Operation Date of the projects in question as also towards carrying cost (pre-COD & post-COD) shall not be enforced and shall be subject to further orders of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 8880/2022 in _Telangana Northern Power Distribution Company Limited & Anr. V. Parampujya Solar Energy Pvt. Limited & Ors., and connected matters_ .
title: Petition under section 79 (1) (a) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Article 10 of the Power Usage Agreements executed between NTPC Ltd. and Telangana State Distribution Companies Limited, seeking compensation due to increase in costs on account of change in rate of Goods & Services Tax as well as increase in basic custom duty amounting to a Change in Law event with respect to the 7 Solar PV Power Project having Project capacity of totalling to 1616 MW under CPSU scheme phase-II tranche-I & II and the tariff was adopted by CERC vide order dated 13.12.2021 in Petition no 174/AT/2021. NTPC Green Energy Ltd.
